componentPlan.focusQuote: Drag depends on the density of the air, the square of the velocity
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Maps explicit dependence of drag on density velocity area and coefficient
Checks recall of equation parts and experimental methods stated on page

overview.headline: Drag force depends on air flow shape and reference area

keyPoints.point: Drag grows with air density and the square of velocity among other factors
keyPoints.quote: Drag depends on the density of the air, the square of the velocity

keyPoints.point: Drag equals drag coefficient times density times half velocity squared times reference area
keyPoints.quote: drag D is equal to the drag coefficient Cd times the density rho (ρ)

keyPoints.point: Drag coefficients are determined experimentally using wind tunnel testing
keyPoints.quote: Drag coefficients are almost always determined experimentally using a wind tunnel.

keyPoints.point: Choice of wing area changes computed coefficient value but total drag stays same
keyPoints.quote: If we choose the wing area, rather than the cross-sectional area, the computed coefficient will have a different value.

keyTerms.gloss: single variable that collects complex dependence for drag
keyTerms.quote: For drag, this variable is called the drag coefficient, designated “Cd.”

keyTerms.gloss: area chosen to characterize dependence of aerodynamic forces
keyTerms.quote: Notice that the area (A) given in the drag equation is given as a reference area.

keyTerms.gloss: mass per volume of air designated by letter rho
keyTerms.quote: In the equation given above, the density is designated by the letter rho (ρ).

keyTerms.gloss: combination of density times square of velocity divided by two
keyTerms.quote: density times the square of the velocity divided by two” is called the dynamic pressure

analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers drag dependencies and drag coefficient, states drag equation relating drag to coefficient density velocity and area, explains reference area choice, density notation and dynamic pressure.
analysis.subject: physics
